Primary error category enum for libheif operations. Values categorize errors such as invalid input, unsupported features, plugin errors, and success. Used as the main code field in heif_error.

Detailed suberror enum complementing heif_error_code. Provides finer-grained reasons for failures (e.g., missing boxes, unsupported features, or encoding problems). Used as the subcode field in heif_error.

Struct describing an error from libheif. Contains a main error code, a detailed suberror code, and a human-readable message that is guaranteed to be non-NULL. Instances may be returned by API calls or provided as constants such as heif_error_success.

objects.definition: LIBHEIF_API extern const heif_error heif_error_success;

Structured set of security limits for libheif operations. Fields cap sizes, counts, and memory usage during parsing/decoding to mitigate resource exhaustion. Version indicates which groups of limits are meaningful. A value of 0 in any limit disables that specific limit.

objects.definition: typedef struct heif_encoder heif_encoder;

objects.definition: typedef struct heif_encoder_parameter heif_encoder_parameter;

objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for reading options used when loading a HEIF context via various read APIs. No definition in this header; details unknown.
Status codes returned by reader callbacks to indicate availability/progress of data when streaming or probing file size/ranges.
Result structure for heif_reader::request_range describing range availability, actual end position, and optional reader-specific error info with message ownership handled via release_error_msg.

Callback vtable that an application implements to let libheif read data from custom sources (files, streams, network). Supports basic read/seek, growing file size checks, optional range prefetching, and error message release.
Callback vtable that an application implements to let libheif write encoded HEIF data to a custom sink (file, stream, etc.). Single write callback plus API version field.

Structure describing tiling metadata for an image or image grid. Contains grid dimensions, tile sizes, full image dimensions, offsets of the top-left tile in transformed coordinates, and optional extra-dimension sizing (e.g., volumetric). Versioned via the 'version' field. Used with decoding/encoding APIs to query or manage tiled images. Destruction not required; it is a plain POD to be stack- or user-allocated and filled by API calls.

Enumeration of allowed compression methods for ISO 23001-17 ("unci") images written via libheif. Values define whether no compression or specific lossless methods (deflate, zlib, brotli) are used. Commented-out entries are not part of this header's API. Used as a field within heif_unci_image_parameters.

Parameter block describing the layout and compression of an ISO 23001-17 (uncompressed/"unci") image to be added to a HEIF file. Includes versioning, image dimensions, tile size, and compression method. Intended to be allocated, copied, and released via the provided API functions; fields may be versioned—unknown details like interleave/padding are noted as TODO.

Placeholder options type for reading images; currently empty in this header.

Abstract output writer interface used by Context::write to emit encoded data.
RAII wrapper for heif_image_handle providing metadata queries, thumbnail access, and image decoding.
Placeholder options for decoding; currently empty.

Placeholder scaling options for Image::scale_image; currently empty.

functions.name: heif_get_version
functions.description: Returns the version string of the linked libheif library. Typical usage: display or log library version for diagnostics or feature gating.

functions.name: heif_get_version_number
functions.description: Returns the numeric version of the linked libheif library encoded as 0xHHMMLL00 (e.g., 0x02150300 for 2.21.3). Use for numeric version comparisons at runtime.

functions.name: heif_get_version_number_major
functions.description: Returns the decimal major version (HH) of the linked libheif.

functions.name: heif_get_version_number_minor
functions.description: Returns the decimal minor version (MM) of the linked libheif.

functions.name: heif_get_version_number_maintenance
functions.description: Returns the decimal maintenance/patch version (LL) of the linked libheif.

functions.name: heif_string_release
functions.description: Frees a NUL-terminated string returned by libheif from various API functions. Safe to pass NULL. Use this to release any libheif-owned strings you obtained.
requirements: Argument may be NULL.
If non-NULL, the pointer must refer to a string that was allocated/returned by libheif.

functions.name: heif_init
functions.description: Initializes the libheif library and loads external codec plugins from the default plugin path. Calls are reference-counted and should be balanced with heif_deinit(). You may pass nullptr for default parameters (currently no parameters are supported).
requirements: Each successful call to heif_init() must be matched by exactly one call to heif_deinit().
The parameter may be NULL (default parameters).
If a non-NULL heif_init_params is provided, it should be initialized; details beyond the presence of a version field are unknown.
Ensure consistent usage across the program (avoid mixing code paths that call init/deinit with those that do not), to prevent using an uninitialized library.

functions.name: heif_deinit
functions.description: Deinitializes and cleans up the libheif library. Balances reference-counted heif_init() calls.
requirements: Must not be called after exit() (e.g., from global C++ destructors), to avoid crashes due to torn-down globals.
Must be called exactly once for each prior successful heif_init() call.

functions.name: heif_load_plugin
functions.signature: LIBHEIF_API heif_error heif_load_plugin(const char* filename, heif_plugin_info const** out_plugin);
functions.description: Loads a single external codec plugin from the given file path and returns information about it. Plugins are currently supported only on Unix platforms.
requirements: Supported on Unix platforms only.
filename must be a valid non-NULL path to a loadable plugin file.
out_plugin must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive a pointer to the loaded plugin info.

functions.name: heif_load_plugins
functions.signature: LIBHEIF_API heif_error heif_load_plugins(const char* directory, const heif_plugin_info** out_plugins, int* out_nPluginsLoaded, int output_array_size);
functions.description: Loads all external codec plugins from the specified directory. Returns an array of loaded plugin infos, and the number loaded, up to the provided output array capacity. Plugins are currently supported only on Unix platforms.
requirements: Supported on Unix platforms only.
directory must be a valid non-NULL directory path.
out_plugins must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an array (or pointer suitable for receiving an array) of plugin info pointers.
out_nPluginsLoaded must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the number of plugins loaded.
output_array_size must specify the capacity of the out_plugins array; must be >= 0 (exact constraints beyond type are not documented).

functions.name: heif_unload_plugin
functions.description: Unloads a previously loaded external plugin. Use on plugin handles obtained from heif_load_plugin() or heif_load_plugins().
requirements: plugin must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a plugin previously returned by heif_load_plugin() or heif_load_plugins().
Supported on Unix platforms only (plugin support limitation).

functions.name: heif_get_plugin_directories
functions.description: Returns a NULL-terminated array of directory paths that libheif searches for plugins, including paths from LIBHEIF_PLUGIN_PATHS and the built-in path (unless overridden). Free the returned array with heif_free_plugin_directories() when done.
requirements: The returned array is NULL-terminated.
The returned pointer should be freed using heif_free_plugin_directories() when no longer needed.

functions.name: heif_free_plugin_directories
functions.description: Frees an array of plugin directory strings previously returned by heif_get_plugin_directories().
requirements: Argument must be a pointer previously returned by heif_get_plugin_directories().

functions.name: heif_register_decoder_plugin
functions.description: Registers a decoder plugin implementation with libheif. Intended for plugins integrated at runtime without dynamic loader helpers. Plugin support is currently only on Unix platforms.
requirements: Argument must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a heif_decoder_plugin structure matching the expected ABI/version (exact fields not documented here).
Supported on Unix platforms only (plugin support limitation).

functions.name: heif_register_encoder_plugin
functions.description: Registers an encoder plugin implementation with libheif. Intended for plugins integrated at runtime without dynamic loader helpers. Plugin support is currently only on Unix platforms.
requirements: Argument must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a heif_encoder_plugin structure matching the expected ABI/version (exact fields not documented here).
Supported on Unix platforms only (plugin support limitation).

functions.name: heif_register_decoder
functions.signature: LIBHEIF_API heif_error heif_register_decoder(heif_context* heif, const heif_decoder_plugin*);
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Registers a decoder plugin on a heif_context. Use heif_register_decoder_plugin(const struct heif_decoder_plugin*) instead.
requirements: Deprecated API; prefer heif_register_decoder_plugin().
heif must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a heif_context.
Second argument must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a heif_decoder_plugin structure matching the expected ABI/version (exact fields not documented here).
Plugin support is currently only on Unix platforms.

functions.name: heif_image_get_colorspace
functions.description: Returns the colorspace of the given decoded image (e.g., YCbCr, RGB, monochrome, nonvisual). Use to branch handling based on colorspace.
requirements: img must point to a valid heif_image instance
The returned value is one of enum heif_colorspace

functions.name: heif_image_get_chroma_format
functions.description: Returns the chroma format of the given image (e.g., 4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, interleaved RGB/RGBA variants).
requirements: img must point to a valid heif_image instance
The returned value is one of enum heif_chroma

functions.name: heif_image_get_width
functions.signature: int heif_image_get_width(const heif_image* img, enum heif_channel channel);
functions.description: Returns the width in pixels of the specified image channel; returns -1 if the channel does not exist.
requirements: img must point to a valid heif_image
channel must be a member of enum heif_channel
Caller must handle return value -1 indicating the channel does not exist

functions.name: heif_image_get_height
functions.signature: int heif_image_get_height(const heif_image* img, enum heif_channel channel);
functions.description: Returns the height in pixels of the specified image channel; returns -1 if the channel does not exist.
requirements: img must point to a valid heif_image
channel must be a member of enum heif_channel
Caller must handle return value -1 indicating the channel does not exist

functions.name: heif_image_get_primary_width
functions.description: Returns the width in pixels of the image’s primary channel (Y for YCbCr/monochrome, any for RGB).
requirements: img must point to a valid heif_image

functions.name: heif_image_get_primary_height
functions.description: Returns the height in pixels of the image’s primary channel (Y for YCbCr/monochrome, any for RGB).
requirements: img must point to a valid heif_image

functions.name: heif_image_crop
functions.signature: heif_error heif_image_crop(heif_image* img, int left, int right, int top, int bottom);
functions.description: Crops an existing image. Details about how left/right/top/bottom are interpreted (pixels to trim vs. rectangle specification) are not documented in this header; assumed to modify img to the cropped region. Usage: call and check returned heif_error.
requirements: img must point to a valid heif_image
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success/failure
Exact semantics of parameters left/right/top/bottom are unknown from this header and should be consulted in library docs/source

functions.name: heif_image_extract_area
functions.signature: heif_error heif_image_extract_area(const heif_image*, uint32_t x0, uint32_t y0, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, const heif_security_limits* limits, heif_image** out_image);
functions.description: Creates a new image that is a rectangular sub-area of the input image at (x0,y0) with size (w,h). Security limits can be provided to control/track allocations. Returns a newly allocated heif_image via out_image.
requirements: Input image pointer must be a valid heif_image
x0 and y0 are the top-left pixel coordinates of the area; w and h are the width and height (units: pixels)

API status: marked experimental in the header

functions.name: heif_context_add_generic_metadata
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_add_generic_metadata(heif_context* ctx, const heif_image_handle* image_handle, const void* data, int size, const char* item_type, const char* content_type);
functions.description: Adds a generic (possibly proprietary) metadata item to the specified image. The item is identified by item_type (e.g., "iptc"). content_type is optional and may be NULL. Suitable for adding IPTC IIM stream data (recommended: item_type="iptc", content_type=NULL).

content_type may be NULL or a valid NUL-terminated string describing the content type
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success/failure

functions.name: heif_context_add_generic_uri_metadata
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_add_generic_uri_metadata(heif_context* ctx, const heif_image_handle* image_handle, const void* data, int size, const char* item_uri_type, heif_item_id* out_item_id);

functions.name: heif_image_handle_has_depth_image

functions.name: heif_encoder_parameter_get_type

functions.name: heif_encoder_parameter_get_valid_integer_range

functions.name: heif_encoder_parameter_integer_valid_range

Check heif_error for success

functions.name: heif_encoder_set_parameter_boolean
functions.signature: heif_error heif_encoder_set_parameter_boolean(heif_encoder*, const char* parameter_name, int value);

requirements: Encoder must be a valid, non-NULL heif_encoder pointer
parameter_name must be a valid, non-NULL string naming a boolean parameter
value is interpreted as boolean (0 or nonzero)
Check heif_error for success

functions.name: heif_encoder_get_parameter_boolean
functions.signature: heif_error heif_encoder_get_parameter_boolean(heif_encoder*, const char* parameter_name, int* value);
functions.description: Gets a boolean parameter by name, returning its value as 0/1.
requirements: Encoder must be a valid, non-NULL heif_encoder pointer
parameter_name must be a valid, non-NULL string naming a boolean parameter
value must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the boolean result

functions.name: heif_encoder_set_parameter_string
functions.signature: heif_error heif_encoder_set_parameter_string(heif_encoder*, const char* parameter_name, const char* value);

Check heif_error for success

functions.name: heif_encoder_get_parameter_string
functions.signature: heif_error heif_encoder_get_parameter_string(heif_encoder*, const char* parameter_name, char* value, int value_size);

Check heif_error for success

parameter_name must be a valid, non-NULL string naming a string parameter

Check heif_error for success

functions.name: heif_encoder_parameter_integer_valid_values
functions.signature: heif_error heif_encoder_parameter_integer_valid_values(heif_encoder*, const char* parameter_name, int* have_minimum, int* have_maximum, int* minimum, int* maximum, int* num_valid_values, const int** out_integer_array);

parameter_name must be a valid, non-NULL string; for encoder-specific passthroughs, use the documented prefix (e.g., "x265:")
value must be a valid, non-NULL string and conform to the parameter’s allowed values
Be aware that prefixed passthrough parameters may skip validation; caller is responsible for correctness
Check heif_error for success

functions.signature: heif_error heif_encoder_get_parameter(heif_encoder*, const char* parameter_name, char* value_ptr, int value_size);

functions.name: heif_context_encode_image
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_encode_image(heif_context*, const heif_image* image, heif_encoder* encoder, const heif_encoding_options* options, heif_image_handle** out_image_handle);
functions.description: Compresses an input image using the given encoder and adds it to the context. Optionally returns a handle to the coded image. The first image added becomes the primary image (can be changed later).
requirements: Context must be a valid, initialized heif_context pointer
image must be a valid, initialized heif_image pointer with content compatible with the encoder

options should be NULL unless you intentionally pass a properly initialized heif_encoding_options
out_image_handle may be NULL to ignore the handle; if non-NULL, it must be a valid pointer to receive the handle
Caller must check heif_error for success
If a handle is returned, manage it per libheif’s handle lifetime rules

functions.name: heif_context_add_overlay_image
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_add_overlay_image(heif_context* ctx, uint32_t image_width, uint32_t image_height, uint16_t nImages, const heif_item_id* image_ids, int32_t* offsets, const uint16_t background_rgba[4], heif_image_handle** out_iovl_image_handle);
functions.description: Creates and adds an overlay (iovl) image that composites multiple images with optional per-image offsets and a background color. Returns a handle to the overlay image if requested.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context pointer
image_width and image_height specify the overlay canvas size and should be positive
nImages is the number of source images to overlay
image_ids must point to an array of length nImages with the item IDs of images to overlay
offsets may be NULL (treated as all zeros) or point to an array of length 2*nImages storing x,y pairs for each image
background_rgba may be NULL for a transparent background; otherwise must point to 4 uint16_t RGBA components
out_iovl_image_handle may be NULL to ignore the result; if non-NULL, must be a valid pointer to receive the handle
Check heif_error for success

functions.name: heif_context_set_primary_image

Check heif_error for success

functions.description: Deprecated: earlier variant of heif_get_encoder_descriptors() that unnecessarily takes a heif_context. Behavior and filtering semantics match the non-context version.
requirements: Context must be a valid heif_context pointer (though not used semantically per comment)
Use format_filter==heif_compression_undefined to match any format
Use name_filter==NULL to match any name
If out_encoders==NULL, the function returns the total number of matching encoders and ignores count
If out_encoders!=NULL, it writes up to count descriptors to out_encoders
Descriptor pointers are owned by libheif; do not free

functions.name: heif_context_set_max_decoding_threads
functions.description: Set the maximum number of threads libheif itself will use during decoding. A value of 0 decodes tiles in the main thread; 1 creates a single background thread; higher values may allow more threading. This only affects libheif’s internal tiling; individual codec plugins may still use their own threading. Typically called before starting any decoding for a context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized heif_context pointer
max_threads should be non-negative; 0 means decode in the main thread; 1 means a single background thread (per the comments)
Call this before starting decoding if you want it to affect subsequent decode operations
No error is returned; the caller cannot directly detect failure

functions.name: heif_have_decoder_for_format
functions.description: Quick capability check for whether at least one decoder is available for the given compression format. Intended to be used before attempting to decode. Availability does not guarantee the decoder can handle all variants of the format.
requirements: format must be a valid value of enum heif_compression_format
Caller must interpret the returned int as a boolean-like indicator (nonzero indicates at least one decoder available; zero indicates none)
Do not assume full coverage of all format variants even if this returns nonzero

functions.name: heif_decoding_options_alloc
functions.description: Allocate and return a heif_decoding_options structure initialized with default values. Always obtain decoding options via this allocator because the struct may grow in future lib versions. Pass the result to decode calls that accept options.
requirements: Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL (allocation failure)
The returned options must be freed with heif_decoding_options_free
Do not stack-allocate or manually size this struct; its size may change across versions

functions.name: heif_decoding_options_copy
functions.description: Copy the contents of a heif_decoding_options from src to dst. Useful for duplicating or modifying default options while preserving versioning details.
requirements: dst must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid heif_decoding_options object (e.g., obtained via heif_decoding_options_alloc)
src must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid heif_decoding_options object
No return value; caller cannot detect failure

functions.name: heif_decoding_options_free
functions.description: Free a heif_decoding_options previously allocated with heif_decoding_options_alloc.
requirements: options must be a pointer previously returned by heif_decoding_options_alloc (or compatible copy semantics); double-free is not allowed
Behavior on options == NULL is not documented here (unknown); caller should avoid passing NULL unless confirmed by the library’s general API conventions

functions.name: heif_get_decoder_descriptors
functions.signature: int heif_get_decoder_descriptors(enum heif_compression_format format_filter, const heif_decoder_descriptor** out_decoders, int count);
functions.description: Retrieve a list of available decoder descriptors, optionally filtered by compression format. If out_decoders is non-NULL, fills up to count entries with pointers to descriptors and returns the number of decoders (no more than count). If out_decoders is NULL, returns the total number of available decoders and ignores count. The list is sorted by decoder priority (plugin-defined).
requirements: format_filter must be a valid enum heif_compression_format; use heif_compression_undefined to get all decoders
If out_decoders != NULL, it must point to writable storage for at least count entries of type const heif_decoder_descriptor*
If out_decoders == NULL, count is ignored and the function returns the total number of decoders
Returned pointers refer to library-managed descriptors; ownership/lifetime is not specified here (unknown); callers should not assume they can free them
count should be non-negative when out_decoders != NULL

functions.name: heif_decoder_descriptor_get_name
functions.description: Return a long, descriptive name (including version information) for the specified decoder descriptor.
requirements: decoder must be a valid pointer to a heif_decoder_descriptor (e.g., obtained from heif_get_decoder_descriptors)
The returned string is const; the caller must not modify or free it
Behavior on decoder == NULL is not documented (unknown); caller should avoid passing NULL

functions.name: heif_decoder_descriptor_get_id_name
functions.description: Return a short, stable, symbolic identifier for the decoder. Intended to remain constant across decoder versions. May return NULL for older plugins that do not provide an ID.
requirements: decoder must be a valid pointer to a heif_decoder_descriptor (e.g., obtained from heif_get_decoder_descriptors)
Caller must handle a NULL return value (older plugins may not supply an ID)
The returned string is const; the caller must not modify or free it

functions.name: heif_decode_image
functions.signature: heif_error heif_decode_image(const heif_image_handle* in_handle, heif_image** out_img, enum heif_colorspace colorspace, enum heif_chroma chroma, const heif_decoding_options* options);
functions.description: Decode an image referenced by a heif_image_handle into a heif_image, applying all geometric transformations specified in the file (rotation, cropping, mirroring). If colorspace or chroma is heif_colorspace_undefined or heif_chroma_undefined, the original values are preserved. Options may be NULL; when provided, obtain them via heif_decoding_options_alloc. Progress callbacks in options may be invoked from background threads.
requirements: in_handle must be a valid, initialized heif_image_handle referencing decodable image data
out_img must be a non-NULL pointer to a heif_image*; on success, *out_img will be set to a decoded image object
colorspace and chroma must be valid enum values; passing heif_colorspace_undefined and/or heif_chroma_undefined selects the source image’s original values
options may be NULL; if non-NULL, it should be allocated/populated via heif_decoding_options_alloc/heif_decoding_options_copy
If progress callbacks are provided in options, they may be called from background threads; progress_user_data and callback implementations must be thread-safe
Caller must check the returned heif_error and handle non-success codes appropriately
Decoding behavior regarding codec plugin threading is independent of libheif’s own thread limit setting

functions.name: heif_image_handle_release
functions.description: Releases a reference to an heif_image_handle. After calling this, the handle must no longer be used. The underlying context is ref-counted, so releasing the handle does not invalidate other handles or the context itself.
requirements: The input handle must be a valid heif_image_handle obtained from libheif APIs.
Do not use the handle after this function returns (treat as destroyed).
It is safe to release the handle even if the originating heif_context was already freed (the handle keeps its own refcount internally).

functions.name: heif_image_handle_is_primary_image
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given image handle refers to the file's primary image; returns 0 otherwise.
requirements: handle must be non-null and refer to a valid heif_image_handle.
Interpret the return value as a boolean (0 = false, non-zero = true).

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_item_id
functions.description: Returns the file-internal item ID associated with this image handle.
requirements: handle must be non-null and valid.
The returned heif_item_id is meaningful only within the associated heif_context/file.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_width
functions.description: Returns the logical image width (pixels). This is the image resolution exposed by the handle (may reflect transformations rather than raw ispe).
requirements: handle must be non-null and valid.
Caller should expect a non-negative integer width; behavior if metadata is missing is not documented here.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_height
functions.description: Returns the logical image height (pixels). This is the image resolution exposed by the handle (may reflect transformations rather than raw ispe).
requirements: handle must be non-null and valid.
Caller should expect a non-negative integer height; behavior if metadata is missing is not documented here.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_has_alpha_channel
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the image has an alpha channel; returns 0 otherwise.
requirements: The input handle must be non-null and valid.
Interpret the return value as boolean (0 = no alpha, non-zero = has alpha).

functions.name: heif_image_handle_is_premultiplied_alpha
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the alpha channel is premultiplied with color channels; returns 0 otherwise.
requirements: The input handle must be non-null and valid.
Interpret the return value as boolean (0 = not premultiplied, non-zero = premultiplied).

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_luma_bits_per_pixel
functions.description: Returns the number of bits per pixel for the luma (Y) component. Only defined for YCbCr or monochrome images. Returns -1 on error or if the information is not present.
requirements: The input handle must be non-null and valid.
Caller must handle a return value of -1 indicating error or unavailable information.
Only expect a meaningful value for images coded in YCbCr or monochrome colorspaces.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_chroma_bits_per_pixel
functions.description: Returns the number of bits per pixel for chroma components. Only defined for YCbCr images. Returns -1 on error or if the information is not present.
requirements: The input handle must be non-null and valid.
Caller must handle a return value of -1 indicating error or unavailable information.
Only expect a meaningful value for images coded in the YCbCr colorspace.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_preferred_decoding_colorspace
functions.signature: heif_error heif_image_handle_get_preferred_decoding_colorspace(const heif_image_handle* image_handle, enum heif_colorspace* out_colorspace, enum heif_chroma* out_chroma);
functions.description: Proposes a colorspace and chroma format to use when decoding this image, aiming to avoid unnecessary colorspace conversions. May return YCbCr or Monochrome, but can also propose RGB (e.g., when matrix_coefficients=0 or native RGB). May return *_undefined if the file lacks sufficient information. Outputs are written via out parameters if the call succeeds.
requirements: image_handle must be non-null and valid.
out_colorspace must be a non-null pointer to receive the proposed heif_colorspace.
out_chroma must be a non-null pointer to receive the proposed heif_chroma.
Caller must check the returned heif_error and only use outputs if it indicates success.
Outputs may be *_undefined if the file lacks necessary metadata.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_ispe_width
functions.description: Returns the image width from the 'ispe' box (the original size without any transformations). Intended for advanced use; do not use unless you know exactly what you are doing.
requirements: handle must be non-null and valid.
Returned value represents the raw ispe width; may differ from logical display width.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_ispe_height
functions.description: Returns the image height from the 'ispe' box (the original size without any transformations). Intended for advanced use; do not use unless you know exactly what you are doing.
requirements: handle must be non-null and valid.
Returned value represents the raw ispe height; may differ from logical display height.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_pixel_aspect_ratio
functions.signature: int heif_image_handle_get_pixel_aspect_ratio(const heif_image_handle*, uint32_t* aspect_h, uint32_t* aspect_v);
functions.description: Retrieves the pixel aspect ratio (PAR) numerator and denominator. Returns non-zero if PAR information exists in the file; returns 0 if not, in which case the outputs are filled with the default 1:1 ratio.
requirements: The input handle must be non-null and valid.
aspect_h must be a non-null pointer to receive the PAR numerator.
aspect_v must be a non-null pointer to receive the PAR denominator.
Caller must handle the return value: 0 means no explicit PAR (outputs set to 1:1).

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_context
functions.description: Returns a context associated with this image handle. The returned context must be released with heif_context_free() regardless of other context pointers you might have. Multiple calls from handles originating from the same file may return different pointers referring to the same logical context; freeing one does not invalidate others.
requirements: handle must be non-null and valid.
The returned heif_context* must be released with heif_context_free() by the caller, in all cases.
It is valid that multiple returned context pointers refer to the same logical context; each must be freed separately.

functions.name: heif_context_alloc
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new libheif heif_context for reading (and possibly writing) HEIF files. Use with corresponding free function when done.
requirements: Must be freed with heif_context_free() to avoid memory leaks.
Returned pointer must be checked for NULL in low-memory situations (standard C practice); specific failure conditions are not documented.

functions.name: heif_context_free
functions.description: Frees a previously allocated heif_context and releases its resources.
requirements: Argument must be a heif_context* previously returned by heif_context_alloc().
Do not call on the same heif_context more than once ("You should not free a context twice.").
After freeing, the pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: heif_context_read_from_file
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_read_from_file(heif_context* ctx, const char* filename, const heif_reading_options* options);
functions.description: Parses a HEIF file from a filesystem path into an existing heif_context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* allocated via heif_context_alloc().
filename must point to a valid, readable file path string.
The heif_reading_options should currently be set to NULL (as documented).
Caller must inspect the returned heif_error for success/failure before using data from ctx.

functions.name: heif_context_read_from_memory
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_read_from_memory(heif_context* ctx, const void* mem, size_t size, const heif_reading_options* options);
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Reads a complete HEIF file provided as an in-memory buffer, copying the data into the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* allocated via heif_context_alloc().
mem must point to a memory buffer of length size containing the entire HEIF file.
size must be the exact number of bytes in mem to read.
The heif_reading_options should currently be set to NULL (as documented).
Caller must check the returned heif_error.
Prefer heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy() instead.

functions.name: heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy(heif_context* ctx, const void* mem, size_t size, const heif_reading_options* options);
functions.description: Reads a complete HEIF file from an in-memory buffer without copying. The buffer must remain valid while the context is in use.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* allocated via heif_context_alloc().
mem must point to a memory buffer of length size containing the entire HEIF file.
size must be the exact number of bytes in mem to read.
The provided memory must be kept alive and unmodified for as long as the heif_context is used ("you will have to keep the memory area alive as long as you use the heif_context").
The heif_reading_options should currently be set to NULL (as documented).
Caller must check the returned heif_error.

functions.name: heif_context_read_from_reader
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_read_from_reader(heif_context* ctx, const heif_reader* reader, void* userdata, const heif_reading_options* options);
functions.description: Reads a HEIF file using a user-supplied streaming reader interface (callbacks) rather than a file or memory buffer. Supports progressive/growing files and optional range prefetching.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* allocated via heif_context_alloc().
reader must point to a valid heif_reader struct with reader_api_version set and required callbacks set as appropriate for the source.

At minimum for linear loading, the callbacks get_position, read, seek, and wait_for_file_size should be implemented as documented in heif_reader comments. Optional range functions may be NULL if not used.
Callbacks must follow the documented return conventions (e.g., read() and seek() return 0 on success).
If request_range returns an error with reader_error_msg, reader.release_error_msg may be called by libheif to free it; implement release_error_msg if non-static strings are returned.
userdata is passed through to all callbacks and may be NULL if your reader does not need it.
The heif_reading_options should currently be set to NULL (as documented).
Caller must check the returned heif_error.

functions.name: heif_context_get_number_of_top_level_images
functions.description: Returns the number of top-level images in the HEIF file represented by ctx. Excludes thumbnails and tile images that form grids.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* that has successfully read a HEIF file.

functions.name: heif_context_is_top_level_image_ID
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the given item ID corresponds to a top-level image in the context; otherwise returns zero.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* with a loaded file.
id is an image item identifier; valid range/values are library-defined and not documented here.

functions.name: heif_context_get_list_of_top_level_image_IDs
functions.signature: int heif_context_get_list_of_top_level_image_IDs(heif_context* ctx, heif_item_id* ID_array, int count);
functions.description: Fills the caller-provided array with up to count top-level image IDs and returns the number of IDs written.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* with a loaded file.
ID_array must be a valid, writable array with space for at least count entries ("user-supplied int-array 'ID_array', preallocated with 'count' entries").
count specifies the maximum number of IDs to write; must be non-negative.

functions.name: heif_context_get_primary_image_ID
functions.description: Retrieves the item ID of the file’s primary image.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* with a loaded file.
id must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the primary image ID.
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success before using the output.

functions.name: heif_context_get_primary_image_handle
functions.description: Returns a handle to the primary image of the HEIF file, i.e., the image that should be displayed by default when multiple images are present.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* with a loaded file.
handle must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the heif_image_handle* result.
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success before using the handle.

functions.name: heif_context_get_image_handle
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_get_image_handle(heif_context* ctx, heif_item_id id, heif_image_handle** handle);
functions.description: Retrieves an image handle for the specified image item ID within the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* with a loaded file.
id must identify an existing image in the context; behavior for invalid IDs is subject to the returned heif_error.
handle must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the heif_image_handle* result.
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success before using the handle.

functions.name: heif_context_debug_dump_boxes_to_file
functions.description: Writes a debug dump of the file’s box structure to the given file descriptor. Output format is for debugging only and not stable.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context*.
fd must be a valid, open file descriptor for writing.
Callers should not rely on the output format; intended for debugging/informational use only.

functions.name: heif_context_write_to_file
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_write_to_file(heif_context* ctx, const char* filename);
functions.description: Writes the contents of the heif_context to a HEIF file at the specified filesystem path.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* prepared for writing (details not specified in this header).
filename must point to a valid, writable file path string.
Caller must check the returned heif_error.

functions.name: heif_context_write
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_write(heif_context* ctx, heif_writer* writer, void* userdata);
functions.description: Writes the heif_context via a user-supplied writer interface. The writer callback receives data chunks to output to the target destination.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context* prepared for writing (details not specified in this header).
writer must be a valid heif_writer with writer_api_version set and write callback provided.
The write callback must return a heif_error; on success its message may be NULL and will be replaced with "Success" by libheif (as documented).
userdata is passed to the writer callback and may be NULL if unused.
Caller must check the returned heif_error.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_image_tiling
functions.signature: heif_error heif_image_handle_get_image_tiling(const heif_image_handle* handle, int process_image_transformations, struct heif_image_tiling* out_tiling);
functions.description: Queries tiling metadata for an image handle and writes it into the provided heif_image_tiling struct. If process_image_transformations is non-zero, returned sizes/offsets reflect any transformations (rotation/crop); otherwise top/left offsets are (0,0). Use this to discover grid layout, tile size, image dimensions, and optional extra dimensions.
requirements: handle must be a valid, non-null pointer to a heif_image_handle that refers to an image (grid or otherwise)
out_tiling must be a non-null pointer to writable memory to receive the tiling data
process_image_transformations is treated as a boolean (0 = false, non-zero = true)
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success before using out_tiling
Version field handling in heif_image_tiling is not documented here; whether the caller must set tiling->version prior to the call is unknown

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_grid_image_tile_id
functions.signature: heif_error heif_image_handle_get_grid_image_tile_id(const heif_image_handle* handle, int process_image_transformations, uint32_t tile_x, uint32_t tile_y, heif_item_id* out_tile_item_id);
functions.description: For a grid image, returns the item ID of a specific grid tile at (tile_x, tile_y). If process_image_transformations is non-zero, the provided tile coordinates are in the transformed image coordinate system and are internally mapped to the original grid.
requirements: handle must be a valid, non-null pointer to a heif_image_handle that refers to a grid image
out_tile_item_id must be non-null and writable
tile_x and tile_y are tile indices (not pixels); they must identify an existing tile in the grid (exact valid range depends on the image’s grid layout)
process_image_transformations is treated as a boolean (0 = false, non-zero = true)
Caller must check the returned heif_error and only use out_tile_item_id on success

functions.name: heif_image_handle_decode_image_tile
functions.signature: heif_error heif_image_handle_decode_image_tile(const heif_image_handle* in_handle, heif_image** out_img, enum heif_colorspace colorspace, enum heif_chroma chroma, const heif_decoding_options* options, uint32_t tile_x, uint32_t tile_y);
functions.description: Decodes a single tile from a grid image identified by in_handle. The tile is specified by tile indices (tile_x, tile_y). If the decoding options specify that transformations are processed (options->ignore_image_transformations == false), the tile indices are given in the transformed coordinate system. The decoded image is returned via out_img in the requested colorspace and chroma format.
requirements: in_handle must be a valid, non-null heif_image_handle referring to a grid image
out_img must be non-null; on success it will receive a pointer to a newly decoded image
colorspace and chroma must be supported by the implementation for the source image; unsupported combinations will yield an error
options may be null; if non-null, its fields must follow libheif’s decoding option rules (details not in this header)
tile_x and tile_y are tile indices (not pixel coordinates) and must select an existing tile
Caller must check the returned heif_error before using *out_img

functions.name: heif_context_encode_grid
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_encode_grid(heif_context* ctx, heif_image** tiles, uint16_t rows, uint16_t columns, heif_encoder* encoder, const heif_encoding_options* input_options, heif_image_handle** out_image_handle);
functions.description: Encodes an array of existing images into a grid image in the given context using the specified encoder. The grid layout is rows × columns, and tiles points to an array of tile images. On success, returns a handle to the created grid image via out_image_handle; the caller must free that handle.
requirements: ctx must be non-null (function returns an error if null)
tiles must be non-null (function returns an error if null) and must reference at least rows*columns images arranged in row-major order (inferred from typical grid usage; exact order not specified)
rows must be > 0 (function returns an error if 0)
columns must be > 0 (function returns an error if 0)
encoder must be non-null (function returns an error if null)
input_options may be null
out_image_handle must be non-null and will receive a handle on success; caller is responsible for freeing the returned handle
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success

functions.name: heif_context_add_grid_image
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_add_grid_image(heif_context* ctx, uint32_t image_width, uint32_t image_height, uint32_t tile_columns, uint32_t tile_rows, const heif_encoding_options* encoding_options, heif_image_handle** out_grid_image_handle);
functions.description: Creates a new (empty) grid image in the context with the specified overall image dimensions and grid layout (tile_columns × tile_rows). Returns a handle to the grid image that can subsequently be populated with tiles using heif_context_add_image_tile.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null heif_context
image_width and image_height should be positive (non-zero) values appropriate for the intended image (inferred from typical constraints; exact limits not specified)
tile_columns and tile_rows should be positive (non-zero) counts defining the grid layout (inferred; exact limits not specified)
encoding_options may be null
out_grid_image_handle must be non-null and writable; on success it receives a handle to the new grid image; caller is expected to free it later
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success before using the handle

functions.name: heif_context_add_image_tile
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_add_image_tile(heif_context* ctx, heif_image_handle* tiled_image, uint32_t tile_x, uint32_t tile_y, const heif_image* image, heif_encoder* encoder);
functions.description: Encodes and adds a single tile image into an existing grid image at tile position (tile_x, tile_y) within the grid. Use this after creating a grid image to populate it with tile images using the specified encoder.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null heif_context
tiled_image must be a valid handle to a grid image previously created (e.g., via heif_context_add_grid_image)
tile_x and tile_y are tile indices and must refer to a valid position within the grid
image must be a valid, non-null heif_image to be encoded as the tile
encoder must be non-null and appropriate for encoding the tile
Caller must check the returned heif_error for success

functions.name: heif_unci_image_parameters_alloc
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new heif_unci_image_parameters structure for configuring an ISO 23001-17 (uncompressed/lossless) image to be written into a HEIF file. Typical usage: call this to obtain a parameters object, fill its fields (e.g., version, image/tile sizes, compression), use it when creating an image, then release it when done. Internals of the structure include fields like version, image_width/height, tile_width/height, and compression.
requirements: No arguments required.
On success, returns a heap-allocated heif_unci_image_parameters pointer; the caller owns it and must release it when no longer needed (see heif_unci_image_parameters_release).
The returned structure’s fields should be initialized/filled appropriately by the caller before use (e.g., set version and dimensions) — specific valid ranges are not documented here.
Thread-safety and lifetime constraints are not documented; avoid sharing the object across threads unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: heif_unci_image_parameters_copy
functions.description: Copies the contents of a heif_unci_image_parameters structure from src to dst. Use this to duplicate parameter sets before modifying them independently.
requirements: dst must point to a valid, writable heif_unci_image_parameters structure.
src must point to a valid, initialized heif_unci_image_parameters structure.
Neither dst nor src may be NULL.
No return value; callers should ensure inputs are valid to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: heif_unci_image_parameters_release
functions.description: Releases a heif_unci_image_parameters structure previously allocated by heif_unci_image_parameters_alloc, freeing associated resources. Call when finished with the parameters object.
requirements: The argument must be a pointer previously returned by heif_unci_image_parameters_alloc (or a copy referring to separately allocated storage, if applicable).
Passing invalid or non-owned pointers leads to undefined behavior.
Whether NULL is allowed is not documented; do not pass NULL unless confirmed elsewhere.

functions.name: heif_context_add_empty_unci_image
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_add_empty_unci_image(heif_context* ctx, const heif_unci_image_parameters* parameters, const heif_encoding_options* encoding_options, const heif_image* prototype, heif_image_handle** out_unci_image_handle);
functions.description: Adds an empty ISO 23001-17 ("uncompressed" or lossless-compressed) image to a HEIF context. No pixel data is written yet; image data is supplied later via heif_context_add_image_tile(). Use this when you need explicit control over tiling/compression rather than the simpler heif_context_encode_image(), which by default disables compression and layout control for this type.
requirements: ctx must be a valid heif_context pointer representing the target HEIF file.
parameters must not be NULL and should describe the image (e.g., version, image_width/height, tile_width/height, and compression).
parameters->compression must be one of the defined enum heif_unci_compression values.
encoding_options is optional and may be NULL.
prototype must not be NULL and must have the same channel configuration as the image data that will be inserted later; the prototype’s image size does not need to match.
out_unci_image_handle must not be NULL; on success it receives a handle to the newly created image. The caller is responsible for releasing this handle using the appropriate libheif release function.

Callers must check the returned heif_error; if ISO 23001-17 images are not supported, the function returns heif_error_Unsupported_feature; it also returns an error if the passed parameters are incorrect.
Actual pixel data must be provided later using heif_context_add_image_tile() before finalizing the file.

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_number_of_text_items
functions.description: Returns the number of text items attached to the given image. Use this to size buffers before retrieving item IDs. Returns zero if the image has no text items.
requirements: image_handle must point to a valid heif_image_handle obtained from the library
Return value is a non-negative count; there is no separate error code for this query

functions.name: heif_image_handle_get_list_of_text_item_ids
functions.signature: int heif_image_handle_get_list_of_text_item_ids(const heif_image_handle* image_handle, heif_item_id* text_item_ids_array, int max_count);
functions.description: Fills the caller-provided array with up to max_count text item identifiers attached to the image. Returns the number of IDs actually written.
requirements: image_handle must point to a valid heif_image_handle obtained from the library
If max_count > 0, text_item_ids_array must be non-null and point to writable storage for at least max_count elements
max_count should be >= 0
Typical usage is to call heif_image_handle_get_number_of_text_items() first to size the array appropriately
The function returns the number of identifiers stored in text_item_ids_array

functions.name: heif_context_get_text_item
functions.signature: heif_error heif_context_get_text_item(const heif_context* context, heif_item_id text_item_id, heif_text_item** out);
functions.description: Retrieves a text item by its identifier from the given context. On success, stores a heif_text_item* in out; the caller must release it with heif_text_item_release().
requirements: context must point to a valid heif_context (e.g., obtained by opening/creating a file)
out must be non-null and point to a location to receive the heif_text_item*
text_item_id must refer to an existing text item in the provided context
On success, the returned heif_text_item must be released by the caller using heif_text_item_release()
Callers must check the returned heif_error and handle non-ok values

functions.name: heif_text_item_get_id
functions.description: Returns the item identifier for the given text item. If text_item is null, returns 0.
requirements: text_item should be a valid heif_text_item obtained from this API and not yet released
If text_item is null, the function returns 0 and no identifier is available

functions.name: heif_text_item_get_content
functions.description: Returns the payload text for the item in the format implied by the associated content_type. The returned string must be released with heif_string_release() when no longer needed.
requirements: text_item should be a valid heif_text_item obtained from this API and not yet released
If text_item is null, the function returns null
The returned const char* must be released by the caller using heif_string_release(); do not free() it
The returned string is read-only until released

functions.name: heif_image_handle_add_text_item
functions.signature: heif_error heif_image_handle_add_text_item(heif_image_handle* image_handle, const char* content_type, const char* text, heif_text_item** out_text_item);
functions.description: Adds a new text item to the specified image with the given content_type and text payload. On success, returns a heif_text_item* via out_text_item representing the newly added item.
requirements: image_handle must be a valid, writable heif_image_handle referencing the target image (exact mutability requirements are not documented here)
content_type must be a non-null pointer to a content type string; its exact allowed values are not specified in this header
text must be a non-null pointer to the text payload; its encoding/format should correspond to content_type (inferred from context)
out_text_item must be non-null and will receive the created heif_text_item on success
On success, the returned heif_text_item must be released by the caller using heif_text_item_release()
Callers must check the returned heif_error and handle non-ok values

functions.name: heif_text_item_release
functions.description: Releases a heif_text_item previously obtained from the API (e.g., via heif_context_get_text_item or creation functions). After release, the item must not be used.
requirements: text_item must have been obtained from this library and not previously released
After this call, text_item and any data derived from it become invalid and must not be accessed

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for ICC profile bytes suitable for heif raw color profile payloads.
# We aim to create valid-looking ICC profiles (rICC/prof) with correct header, tag table,
# and at least one or two common tags. This should increase likelihood of libheif accepting
# the profile without errors. Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

ICC_SIGNATURE = b'acsp'  # ICC profile signature

# Common PCS and color space signatures
PCS_LIST = [b'XYZ ', b'Lab ', b'XYZ ']
COLOR_SPACE_LIST = [b'RGB ', b'GRAY', b'XYZ ']

# Common profile/device/class signatures
PROFILE_CLASS_LIST = [b'display ', b'output  ', b'input   ', b'colorspc']

RENDERING_INTENT = [0, 1, 2, 3]

# Minimal tag payload helpers

def pad4(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    pad = (4 - (len(b) % 4)) % 4
    return b + (b"\x00" * pad)


def u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", n)


def u16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", n)


def s15Fixed16(value: float) -> bytes:
    # Clamp to reasonable range
    v = max(-32768.0, min(32767.9999, value))
    integer = int(v)
    frac = int(round((v - integer) * 65536)) & 0xFFFF
    return struct.pack(">hH", integer, frac)


def XYZType(x=0.9642, y=1.0000, z=0.8249) -> bytes:
    # iccTypeSignature 'XYZ ' + reserved + 3 * XYZNumber (s15Fixed16)
    b = b"XYZ " + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"
    for comp in (x, y, z):
        b += s15Fixed16(comp) + s15Fixed16(0.0)  # XYZNumber uses 32.32? In ICC it's 16.16 per component.
    return b


def descType(text: str) -> bytes:
    # Use modern 'desc' type with ASCII description
    raw = text.encode('ascii', 'ignore')[:128]
    # ICC descType: signature 'desc', reserved, asciiCount, asciiString, then 0 length unicode/ScriptCode
    ascii_part = u32(len(raw)) + raw
    # pad to 4
    ascii_part = pad4(ascii_part)
    return b"desc" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" + ascii_part + u32(0) + u32(0) + u16(0) + u16(0)


def curvType(gamma: float) -> bytes:
    # curveType: 'curv' + reserved + count + entries (u16)
    # Use single gamma approximated entry count 1 with value scaled
    val = int(max(0, min(65535, round(gamma * 256))))
    body = u32(1) + u16(val)
    return b"curv" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" + body


def rXYZ_tag() -> bytes:
    return XYZType(0.4360747, 0.2225045, 0.0139322)


def gXYZ_tag() -> bytes:
    return XYZType(0.3850649, 0.7168786, 0.0971045)


def bXYZ_tag() -> bytes:
    return XYZType(0.1430804, 0.0606169, 0.7141733)


def generate_icc(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Profile header (128 bytes)
    # We'll construct tags, then fill size and other fields

    # Build a small set of tags. Select from common tags to look valid.
    tags = []  # List[tuple(tagSig: bytes, payload: bytes)]

    # Description tag 'desc'
    desc_texts = [
        "sRGB IEC61966-2.1",
        "Generic RGB Profile",
        "Linear RGB",
        "Display Profile",
    ]
    desc_payload = descType(rnd.choice(desc_texts))
    tags.append((b'desc', desc_payload))

    # White point tag 'wtpt' XYZ
    wtpt_payload = XYZType(0.9642, 1.0, 0.8249)
    tags.append((b'wtpt', wtpt_payload))

    # Primaries (rXYZ, gXYZ, bXYZ)
    tags.append((b'rXYZ', rXYZ_tag()))
    tags.append((b'gXYZ', gXYZ_tag()))
    tags.append((b'bXYZ', bXYZ_tag()))

    # Tone reproduction curves for R,G,B (curv)
    gamma_choices = [1.0, 2.2, 2.4]
    gamma = rnd.choice(gamma_choices)
    tags.append((b'rTRC', curvType(gamma)))
    tags.append((b'gTRC', curvType(gamma)))
    tags.append((b'bTRC', curvType(gamma)))

    # Assemble tag table and payload blob
    payload_blob = b""
    entries = []  # (sig, offset, size)
    # Tag table comes immediately after header + tagCount*12 + 4(count)

    # First, compute header (placeholder) and table sizes to calculate offsets
    tag_count = len(tags)
    tag_table_size = 4 + tag_count * 12
    offset = 128 + tag_table_size

    for sig, pl in tags:
        pl_padded = pad4(pl)
        entries.append((sig, offset, len(pl)))
        payload_blob += pl_padded
        offset += len(pl_padded)

    profile_size = 128 + tag_table_size + len(payload_blob)

    # Construct header fields per ICC v2/4 basics
    # size (u32), cmmId (4), version (1 byte major<<4), deviceClass(4), colorSpace(4), pcs(4), dateTime(12),
    # signature('acsp'), platform(4), flags(4), manufacturer(4), model(4), attributes(8), intent(4),
    # illuminant XYZ (12 s15Fixed16), creator(4), reserved(44)

    cmm = b'LCMS'  # arbitrary
    version_major = 4 if rnd.random() < 0.7 else 2
    version = bytes([version_major << 4, 0, 0, 0])
    device_class = rnd.choice(PROFILE_CLASS_LIST)
    color_space = rnd.choice(COLOR_SPACE_LIST)
    pcs = rnd.choice(PCS_LIST)

    # Simple fixed datetime (2000-01-01 00:00:00)
    dt = struct.pack(">6H", 2000, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)

    platform = b'APPL'
    flags = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"
    manufacturer = b'NONE'
    model = b'NONE'
    attributes = b"\x00" * 8
    intent = u32(rnd.choice(RENDERING_INTENT))
    illuminant = s15Fixed16(0.9642) + s15Fixed16(1.0) + s15Fixed16(0.8249)
    creator = b'pyic'
    reserved = b"\x00" * 44

    header = b"".join([
        u32(profile_size),
        cmm,
        version,
        device_class,
        color_space,
        pcs,
        dt,
        ICC_SIGNATURE,
        platform,
        flags,
        manufacturer,
        model,
        attributes,
        intent,
        illuminant,
        creator,
        reserved,
    ])
    # Ensure header is 128 bytes
    if len(header) != 128:
        # Adjust if lengths differ (defensive, should not happen)
        header = header.ljust(128, b"\x00")[:128]

    # Tag table
    table = u32(tag_count)
    for sig, off, size in entries:
        table += sig + u32(off) + u32(size)

    icc = header + table + payload_blob
    # Final size guard
    if len(icc) > 4096:
        icc = icc[:4096]
        # Fix size field
        icc = u32(len(icc)) + icc[4:]
    return icc


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a valid ICC profile blob appropriate for both rICC and prof fourcc usage.
    return generate_icc(seed)

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces ISO BMFF headers starting at offset 0 and containing
# a valid ftyp box with configurable major brand, minor version, and a list of
# compatible brands. The resulting bytes are valid enough for libheif brand
# parsing, filetype probing, and memory-based reads that expect at least an ftyp.
#
# Constraints from fuzz stubs:
# - heif_read_main_brand / heif_main_brand: need >=12 bytes; our ftyp is >= 16.
# - heif_read_minor_version_brand: needs >=16 bytes; satisfied.
# - heif_has_compatible_brand / heif_list_compatible_brands / heif_check_filetype /
#   heif_has_compatible_filetype: expect data starting at ftyp; satisfied.
# - heif_context_read_from_memory* and C++ Context reads: may accept minimal files; we
#   still provide just ftyp (valid header). Some paths may report unsupported or need
#   more data, which is fine; the buffer is valid and small.

# Common HEIF/AVIF brands to exercise different code paths
COMMON_BRANDS = [
    b"heic", b"heix", b"hevc", b"hevx", b"mif1", b"msf1",
    b"avif", b"avis", b"vvic", b"vvis", b"evbi", b"evbs",
    b"j2ki", b"j2is"
]

# Add some generic ISO brands often found in BMFF to broaden compatibility lists
GENERIC_BRANDS = [
    b"iso5", b"isom", b"mp41", b"mp42", b"miaf", b"MA1B", b"MA1A"
]

ALL_BRANDS = COMMON_BRANDS + GENERIC_BRANDS


def _pick_brands(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[bytes, int, List[bytes]]:
    # Choose a major brand from full set, bias towards HEIF/AVIF brands
    major = rng.choice(ALL_BRANDS if rng.random() < 0.8 else [b"isom", b"mp41", b"mp42"])  # 4 bytes
    # Minor version as uint32
    # Use a mix of common values and random ones
    common_minor = [0, 0x200, 0x01000000, 0x00010000, 0x00000001]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        minor = rng.choice(common_minor)
    else:
        minor = rng.getrandbits(32)
    # Compatible brands: ensure at least the major brand is present sometimes
    n = rng.randint(1, 16)  # keep short; ftyp stays small (< 4096)
    compat = []
    pool = list(ALL_BRANDS)
    rng.shuffle(pool)
    for _ in range(n):
        if pool:
            compat.append(pool.pop())
        else:
            # fallback random fourcc letters/digits
            word = bytes(rng.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789") for _ in range(4))
            compat.append(word)
    # Occasionally insert the major brand into compat if not present
    if rng.random() < 0.7 and major not in compat:
        compat[rng.randrange(len(compat))] = major
    return major, minor, compat


def _make_ftyp(major: bytes, minor: int, compat: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Box: size(4) + type(4) + major_brand(4) + minor_version(4) + compat*(4)
    payload = major + struct.pack(">I", minor)
    for c in compat:
        # Ensure exactly 4 bytes per brand; if not, coerce
        c4 = (c + b"    ")[:4]
        payload += c4
    size = 8 + len(payload)
    return struct.pack(">I4s", size, b"ftyp") + payload


def _maybe_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Optionally add harmless leading boxes before ftyp is not allowed by spec; ftyp must be first.
    # So we do not prefix any other box to keep strict validity for brand readers.
    return b""


def _maybe_suffix_boxes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Optionally add a minimal free box or meta-like placeholder to vary lengths, still valid BMFF.
    boxes = []
    # Add a free box sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        free_payload_len = rng.randint(0, 64)
        size = 8 + free_payload_len
        boxes.append(struct.pack(">I4s", size, b"free") + rng.randbytes(free_payload_len))
    # Add a wide box sometimes (64-bit size) but keep it minimal and small
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        # 1 indicates 64-bit largesize follows; type 'uuid' with 16-byte user type
        user = rng.randbytes(16)
        payload = b""  # keep empty
        largesize = 16 + 8 + 16 + len(payload)  # size(4)+type(4)+largesize(8)+usertype(16)+payload
        boxes.append(struct.pack(">I4sQ16s", 1, b"uuid", largesize, user) + payload)
    return b"".join(boxes)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a valid ftyp box
    major, minor, compat = _pick_brands(rng)
    ftyp = _make_ftyp(major, minor, compat)

    # Optionally extend with additional valid boxes to vary sizes
    suffix = _maybe_suffix_boxes(rng)

    blob = _maybe_prefix(rng) + ftyp + suffix

    # Ensure size constraints for the fuzzing harness
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]

    # Some stubs also pass this buffer as a filename via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME in other contexts;
    # however, in our provided targets only bytes are consumed. We just return the bytes.
    return blob

import struct
import string

# Generator for inputs targeting libheif fuzzers focusing on FourCC strings and minimal ISO BMFF headers
# Covered stubs:
# - heif_fourcc_to_brand: needs >=4 chars, only first 4 used
# - heif_has_compatible_brand: buffer that may contain an ftyp box; brand string of 4 chars
# - heif_context_add_generic_metadata: needs a 4-char item_type (printable), optional content_type, and payload

# blob for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME calls; providing structured, valid-looking data increases
